story_type: boat sank, lone boater clinging to a bait box in rough open water, swimmer and helicopter hoist
hook: His boat sank. A bait box was all he had left to hold.
narration: His boat sank in the channel off Molokai, and a bait box was all he had left to hold on to.
The twenty-nine-foot Hana Hou took on water and went down in the Kaiwi Channel.
At five forty in the morning, Coast Guard watchstanders in Honolulu heard two mayday calls.
Watchstanders at Sector Honolulu sent helicopter crews out over the channel to search for him.
Four hours later, at nine thirty-seven, the second helicopter crew spotted one man in the water.
He was about two miles southwest of Ilio Point, in a sea full of whitecaps.
[short pause] The crew lowered a rescue swimmer to him on the cable.
The swimmer does the hard work in the water, so the helicopter can hold a steady hover above the waves.
outcome: The Dolphin crew from Air Station Barbers Point hoisted the fifty-nine-year-old up out of the sea.
title: Boat sank, he clung to a bait box
description:
On June 24, 2025, a Coast Guard Air Station Barbers Point MH-65 Dolphin crew rescued a 59-year-old man clinging to a bait box after his boat sank about 2 miles southwest of Ilio Point, Molokai, Hawaii.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video, courtesy Air Station Barbers Point, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/967967/coast-guard-rescues-1-water-near-molokai
